task.description:
This is a MANDATORY sign-off per ISS-0430's own acceptance criterion 4 ('Tenant isolation is addressed as a security property, not a naming convention -- the design names the mechanism preventing tenant A's notification reaching tenant B's listener, and SECURITY-REVIEWER signs off on it as a tenant-data-path change'), even though this is a DESIGN-ONLY artefact with zero implementation (lib/letflow/design/iss0430-notify-listen-decision.md, gated PASS by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at handoffs/WF03-ISS0430-20260905/step-02b-code-design-validator.json). Read docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md in full, focusing on INV-1 (tenant data isolation, BLOCKER severity, schema-per-tenant via Ecto :prefix, per docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md Dimension B).

Read the design artefact's Question 2 section ('Multi-tenancy (the hardest part)') in full -- this is the section your sign-off is against. The design proposes: a single, database-global, shared NOTIFY channel (or small fixed set of channels, one per wake-up category); a NOTIFY payload that is always a bare opaque routing id (a row's own per-tenant-schema primary key) and NEVER tenant-identifying data, schema name, or row content; and a receiving process that never trusts the payload directly -- it re-derives its own already-known tenant :prefix scope and does a normal Ecto :prefix-scoped fetch, discarding any id that resolves to nothing under that scope. The design also argues the sequential-id cross-tenant-enumeration risk is structurally defused because Letflow's schema-per-tenant model gives each tenant's own table its own physical Postgres sequence object (no shared cross-tenant id ordering to correlate).

Independently verify this reasoning against INV-1 and against decision 0003's actual mechanism -- do not accept the design's or CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own conclusion on trust; re-derive your own verdict, per core-directives.md's 'Every producing step has a validating step' (a validator that echoes a prior validator's PASS has not validated anything). Specifically assess: (a) does this mechanism actually prevent tenant A's notification from being usable as tenant B's data, given Postgres NOTIFY has no schema/:prefix scoping at all (confirm this is true of Postgres's actual documented behavior, don't take the design's word for it); (b) is 'payload carries only an opaque id, receiver re-derives its own :prefix' a sufficient structural guarantee, or does it merely relocate the risk somewhere the design hasn't examined (e.g. could a future careless consumer implementation accidentally derive its :prefix FROM the NOTIFY payload or channel instead of from its own already-known scope, defeating the invariant -- if so, does the design's own stated invariants I1/I2 section adequately warn against that for a future implementer); (c) is the sequential-id enumeration argument (disjoint per-schema sequences) actually sound, i.e. does Letflow truly provision one physical sequence per tenant schema under its actual TenantProvisioning mechanism (cite the real provisioning code/migration if you can find it, don't just accept the design doc's citation of decision 0003's prose); (d) is there any OTHER tenant-data leak vector the design didn't consider (e.g. NOTIFY's own transport is unencrypted database-session traffic already covered by Postgres's normal connection security -- is there a new attack surface being introduced, such as any process on the same OS host being able to open a raw connection and LISTEN on the shared channel to observe cross-tenant activity timing, and if so does the design need to say more about it, or is that already covered by ordinary Postgres access control which is out of this design's scope). State explicitly which of INV-1 through INV-9 apply and your verdict against each, per the security-invariants.md 'How to verify' sections and the SECURITY-REVIEWER worked example in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md (a verdict per invariant, APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE stated for each, not just the ones that seem relevant).
acceptance_criteria: Verdict stated against every invariant INV-1..INV-9 (APPLIES-and-PASS, APPLIES-and-FAIL, or NOT-APPLICABLE with reason), not only INV-1
INV-1's verdict is independently re-derived, not copied from CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's or CODE-DESIGNER's own reasoning
Confirms or corrects, with evidence, whether Postgres NOTIFY genuinely has no schema/:prefix scoping (the load-bearing premise of the design's whole tenant-isolation answer)

Assesses whether the opaque-id/receiver-re-derives-scope structural guarantee could be defeated by a future careless implementation, and whether the design's own stated invariants (I1/I2) adequately guard against that
Assesses the sequential-id enumeration argument's factual soundness against Letflow's actual tenant-schema provisioning mechanism, citing real code/migrations if locatable
States whether any additional tenant-data leak vector exists that the design did not consider
PASS or FAIL/BLOCKER stated explicitly with evidence; on FAIL, next_action names CODE-DESIGNER for rework with the exact gap

result.summary: PASS. Independently re-derived against lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, priv/repo/migrations/20260829020001_create_timers.exs, priv/repo/migrations/20260902010001_create_service_task_dispatches.exs, priv/repo/migrations/20260816120001_create_events.exs, and Postgres's own documented NOTIFY semantics directly -- not the design's or CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own conclusions. (a) CONFIRMED: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY has zero schema/:prefix/search_path scoping -- a database-global channel namespace where every backend that issued LISTEN <channel> receives every NOTIFY <channel> on that database regardless of the firing transaction's schema. The design's load-bearing premise is factually accurate. Given this, pushing 100% of actual tenant-isolation enforcement onto decision 0003's existing :prefix-scoped fetch (never inventing a NOTIFY-layer isolation mechanism that cannot exist) is the correct response, not a workaround. (b) The opaque-id/receiver-re-derives-its-own-:prefix guarantee is structurally sound but has no automated enforcement yet -- a future careless consumer COULD derive :prefix from the NOTIFY payload/channel instead of its own already-known scope, defeating the invariant. The design's I1 (payload never carries tenant-identifying data) and I2 (consumer always re-derives its own scope, never from the NOTIFY message) state this in checkable, imperative form and are adequate as a warning to a future implementer, but they are prose invariants, not a lint/test gate -- flagged as a forward obligation: whichever future ELIXIR-DEV handoff implements the actual Letflow.Notify.Listener consumer requires its own INV-1 SECURITY-REVIEWER pass checking the real :prefix derivation in that code, exactly as the design's own Question 2 verdict section (lines 336-340) and ISS-0430 AC4 already require -- this is not a gap in this design-only sign-off, it is correctly deferred. (c) Sequential-id enumeration argument verified against REAL code, not the design doc's citation of decision 0003's prose: lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's provision_tenant_schema/1 (line 273) issues CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS for a physically distinct Postgres schema per tenant, and replay_migrations/2 (lines 334-338) runs Ecto.Migrator.run(Repo, migrations, :up, prefix: schema_name, ...) against that schema -- confirming schema-per-tenant is actually implemented, not just decided in prose. Read the two migrations the design's own Question 3 table cites by name: both create table(..., primary_key: false, prefix: prefix()) with add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true -- UUID primary keys, not Postgres serial/sequence-backed integers. Grepped every migration in priv/repo/migrations/*.exs for a non-binary_id :id column: zero found -- every table's id is a UUID, making the enumeration risk moot for the design's own two illustrative payload examples (timers.id, service_task_dispatches.id) by an even stronger route than the design's stated argument. Separately confirmed the design's general disjoint-per-schema-sequence claim is ALSO factually sound where sequences do exist: 20260816120001_create_events.exs defines add :global_seq, :bigserial, null: false inside a prefix: prefix()-scoped create table, so Postgres creates that bigserial's owning sequence object physically inside each tenant's own schema -- no shared cross-tenant sequence exists anywhere in this codebase. The design's factual claim checks out and is stronger than stated for the tables actually in scope. (d) No additional leak vector found. OS-level raw-connection LISTEN access is gated by ordinary Postgres connection/authentication access control, the same trust boundary as any other Postgres client connection -- not a new attack surface NOTIFY introduces, and appropriately out of this design's scope. Channel-name introspection (pg_stat_activity/pg_listening_channels()) leaking tenant existence is already addressed by the design's own rejection of option (b) (per-tenant channel names) for exactly this reason. VERDICT PER INVARIANT, INV-1 THROUGH INV-9: INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS, independently re-derived per (a)/(b)/(c) above. INV-2 (server-side field authorisation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE, no API response type touched, no consumer exists (Question 6: not retrofitted now), real-time push to web/ explicitly out of ISS-0430's scope. INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing) -- NOT-APPLICABLE, S5 not started, no Lua/WASM surface touched. INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES, PASS: design reuses Letflow.Repo's existing connection config for the new Postgrex.Notifications connection (Cross-module dependencies section), introduces no new secret material, logs, or serialized credential. INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) -- NOT-APPLICABLE, no lookup-by-ID endpoint exists or is proposed, S4 not started. INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES, PASS: this handoff itself, verdicting every applicable invariant with concrete evidence, is the proof artefact INV-6 requires. INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, PASS: the design document itself contains zero SQL/code (confirmed by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and independently re-confirmed here reading the full artefact); the one raw-SQL identifier interpolation in the codebase's real precedent (tenant_provisioning.ex line 273, CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "#{schema_name}") is pre-existing code outside this handoff's diff, already justified by schema_name's constrained shape via Ecto.UUID.cast/1. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES, PASS: no implementation exists yet to grep, but the design's Question 4 explicitly reasons through NOTIFY's fire-and-forget failure modes (lost notifications, commit-only delivery, connection churn) and mandates polling remain the unconditional reconciliation backstop specifically because NOTIFY cannot be trusted as sole delivery -- the correct architectural posture for INV-8's concern even pre-implementation. INV-9 (tenant-controlled outbound URL validation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE, this design makes no outbound HTTP request, concerns only in-process Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY. No FAIL on any applicable invariant.
result.next_action: Route to ORCH: SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off complete and PASSING for ISS-0430's design artefact (lib/letflow/design/iss0430-notify-listen-decision.md), satisfying ISS-0430 AC4. Per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own next_action (step-02b), no ELIXIR-DEV/FRONTEND-DEV implementation follow-on is in scope -- ISS-0430 explicitly scopes 'implementation is separate follow-on work'. ORCH should close out this WF-03 run against the design artefact. Forward obligation recorded for whichever future requirement implements Letflow.Notify.Listener's actual consumer: that implementation requires its own INV-1 SECURITY-REVIEWER pass checking the real :prefix derivation in the shipped code, per this design's own I1/I2 and ISS-0430 AC4's own stated implementation-time deferral -- not a gap in this sign-off, but should not be silently skipped when that future work is scoped.
